# openinfra_certificate_authority (Resource)

A managed private certificate authority — the ACM-Private-CA-shaped primitive. Each CA is a Vault PKI mount that issues short-lived leaf certificates for names under the domains you allow; stand up a self-signed `root`, or an `intermediate` signed by one. Issue and revoke from the console (EXPERIMENTAL; requires the encryption component + Vault).



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `common_name` (String) The CA certificate's subject common name. Baked into the CA cert, so it replaces.
- `name` (String) Resource name. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `allowed_domains` (List of String) Domains the CA's `issuer` role may issue for; subdomains are allowed.
- `hierarchy` (String) `root` (self-signed) or `intermediate` (signed by `parent`). Fixed at creation.
- `key_type` (String) `rsa-2048`, `rsa-4096`, `ec-256` or `ec-384`. The CA key algorithm, fixed at creation.
- `max_ttl` (String) Ceiling on the CA cert's lifetime and on issued leaf TTLs, as a Go duration (e.g. `8760h`).
- `namespace` (String) Kubernetes namespace. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `parent` (String) Name of the parent `openinfra_certificate_authority`, required when `hierarchy = intermediate`.

### Read-Only

- `ca_cert_pem` (String) The CA certificate, PEM. Distribute to trust stores.
- `id` (String) `namespace/name`, the import identifier.
- `not_after` (String) The CA certificate's expiry.
- `pki_mount` (String) The Vault mount path, `pki-<name>`.
- `ready` (Boolean) Whether the resource's Ready condition is True. Terraform returns as soon as the object is accepted, so this is usually `false` immediately after apply — the platform reconciles asynchronously.
- `serial` (String) The CA certificate's serial number.
